turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Well, Dr. Smith, I'm... I'm here because things have been really strange at work lately. Ever since I won that county safety award—which, by the way, they gave me this little glass plaque, but the engraving was slightly crooked, and I remember thinking, 'Is this a joke?' Like, my uncle had a trophy shop back in Ohio, and he would never let something like that out the door. He was a real stickler. Anyway, ever since that award, certain people at the transportation depot have been twisting my inspection reports. They keep asking these really pointed budget questions, acting like I'm doing something crooked. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just a 'normal review process,' but... I mean, I know what a normal review looks like. I've been doing this since I got out of high school. It's obvious there's this coordinated effort to discredit me. Just like how my neighbor keeps parking his truck two inches over my property line. It's all about pushing boundaries, you know? But yeah, the work thing... that's why they told me to come talk to you.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that coworkers are engaged in a coordinated effort to discredit him, despite his supervisor's reassurance that it is just a normal review process.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, I don't hear anything like that. My hearing is actually really sharp. I had to get it tested a couple of years ago for a DOT physical, back when I was thinking about getting my commercial driver's license instead of just inspecting. 

The clinic they sent me to was over on 4th Street, right next to this amazing Italian deli. They make this meatball sub that is just... unbelievable. The sauce is super sweet, which you wouldn't think works, but it totally does. I tried making it at home once, but tomatoes are so expensive right now. Have you noticed that? The produce section is just a complete rip-off lately. I ended up trying to grow my own in some buckets on my balcony, but the pigeons kept getting to them. Pigeons are actually incredibly smart, honestly, they remember faces. If you shoo them away once, they'll come back and specifically target your car. 

But anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, voices. No, no imaginary voices or sounds or anything. Just the normal stuff.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and derailment, wandering from a hearing test to a deli, tomatoes, and pigeons before finally returning to the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing imaginary voices or sounds.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel like you have been treated unfairly or taken advantage of in other areas of your life outside of your current workplace, such as with friends or family members?
turns.patient_response:
Treated unfairly? By my family or friends? No, no, nothing like that. They're fine. Actually, my buddy Dave just helped me move this giant couch I bought last weekend. Man, that thing was incredibly heavy. It's one of those sectionals with the recliners built in? We had to take the front door off the hinges just to get it inside my apartment. 

Which reminds me, I still need to fix that bottom hinge. The screws got completely stripped. You ever try to get a stripped screw out of a door frame? It's a total nightmare. I saw this trick on YouTube where you put a rubber band over the screw head to get more grip with the drill, but it didn't work at all. The rubber band just snapped and hit me right in the knuckle. Hurt like crazy. I really think half of YouTube is just people making stuff up for views anyway. Like those videos of guys building entire underground swimming pools in the jungle with just a stick? There's no way they don't have a backhoe parked right off camera. It's all completely staged. 

But... wait, what did you ask me? Did Dave do something? No, Dave's a good guy, we're good.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and derailment, drifting from a friend helping them move to door hinges, stripped screws, and fake YouTube videos before forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies feeling treated unfairly or taken advantage of by family or friends.

turns.doctor_question: Have you always felt that people in your life, even before this recent situation at work, were generally untrustworthy or out to get you?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. I mean, before this whole thing at the depot, I didn't really think about people being untrustworthy. I just went to work, did my job, went home. I used to go to this bowling league on Thursday nights before they closed the alley down. It's a shame, too, because they had the best shoe rental prices in town. Now it's some sort of boutique fitness center where people pay fifty bucks to ride a stationary bike in the dark. I don't get it. Why would you pay that much to sit in a dark room and pedal nowhere? You could just buy a real bike and ride it outside for free. 

I bought a mountain bike a few years ago at a garage sale. The guy said it was barely used, but the chain was completely rusted out. I spent an entire Saturday trying to soak it in WD-40, which, by the way, isn't actually a lubricant, it's a water displacer. A lot of people don't know that. If you really want to grease a chain, you need a proper silicone-based... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, untrustworthy people. No, before the award and the inspection reports, I never really felt like anyone was out to get me. It's just this specific group at work right now.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient confirms a current belief that a specific group of people at work is out to get them, indicating a persecutory delusion.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, wandering off-topic to discuss bowling, fitness centers, bicycles, and WD-40 before returning to the doctor's question.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that this coordinated effort to discredit you at work is connected to a larger group or organization, such as a government agency or a secret society?
turns.patient_response:
A government agency? Like a secret society? No, man, nothing crazy like that. It's just the guys at the depot—my supervisors and the other inspectors. Why would the government care about my inspection reports? 

I mean, dealing with the government is a headache anyway. Have you been to the DMV lately? I had to go last month to renew the registration on my truck, and the line was literally out the door before they even opened. I stood there for two hours just to hand a lady a single piece of paper. And the parking lot there is a complete disaster. Potholes everywhere. It's ironic, really, the Department of Motor Vehicles having a parking lot that completely wrecks your suspension. I actually had to get my alignment checked after hitting one of those craters. 

Took it to this shop on Elm, and the mechanic tried to tell me I needed four brand new tires. I looked at the tread myself, they've got at least another ten thousand miles on them. Those guys are always trying to upsell you on something. You go in for a basic oil change and suddenly you need a new air filter, a cabin filter, a transmission flush... it's a total scam. If you don't know cars, they'll rob you blind. My dad taught me how to change my own brake pads when I was sixteen, which has saved me so much money over the years. You just need a C-clamp to compress the caliper piston so you can fit the new pads in, otherwise they won't slide over the rotor... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Secret societies? No, no. No men in black or anything. It's just the guys at work trying to push me out.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient maintains a fixed persecutory belief that his coworkers and supervisors are actively trying to push him out and discredit him.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, wandering off-topic from government agencies to the DMV, potholes, mechanics, and brake pads before finally recalling the original question.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your life, have you often felt like you had to be constantly on guard because others were trying to take advantage of you, deceive you, or harm you, even in situations where there was no clear evidence of it?
turns.patient_response:
On guard? Like my whole life? No, I never really felt like that. I don't walk around looking over my shoulder or anything. Speaking of being on guard, though, they just hired this new security guard at the grocery store down the street from my place. The guy stands by the sliding doors in full tactical gear just to watch people buy produce. It's ridiculous. He's got the heavy vest, the radio earpiece, the whole nine yards. Like, buddy, nobody is trying to pull a heist on the organic avocados. 

They are way too expensive to buy anyway. Have you seen the price of groceries lately? I went in for just eggs and milk the other day and it was almost twenty bucks. And the eggs weren't even the large ones, they were those weird medium ones that come in the cheap cardboard carton that always tears when you try to open it. I hate those cartons. You pull the little tab and it just rips half the lid off, so you can never close it right again. Then they just sit open in your fridge and get that weird fridge smell. You know what I'm talking about? Baking soda is supposed to fix that, but I bought a box of Arm & Hammer and just left it in the back for a year, and I don't think it did a single thing. You're supposed to change it every thirty days, but who actually remembers to do that? I should probably set a reminder on my phone or something... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being on guard. No, I never felt like people were trying to deceive me or whatever before this mess at the depot. I've always been a pretty relaxed guy.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from the topic of being on guard to a local security guard, grocery prices, egg cartons, and baking soda before losing track of the original question.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you felt that your coworkers have been working against you in this way?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it's been about a year now. It all started right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. They gave me this little plaque, which was nice, I guess, but it was made of that really cheap particle board stuff with a fake wood veneer glued over it. You know the kind? Like the furniture you buy at those big box stores that you have to assemble yourself with that tiny little hex key. 

I bought a bookshelf from one of those places once, and I swear it took me four hours to put it together. The instructions didn't have any words, just these confusing little diagrams of a guy smiling while holding a screwdriver. And halfway through, I realized I had put the middle shelf in backward, so the unfinished edge was facing out. I had to take the whole thing apart just to flip that one piece. It drove me crazy. And then, when I finally got it done and put my books on it, the shelves immediately started sagging in the middle. I mean, what's the point of a bookshelf that can't hold books? I ended up using it to store my old DVDs instead. 

I've still got a huge collection of DVDs. Mostly action movies from the nineties. They just don't make movies like that anymore, with real practical effects and actual explosions. Now everything is just computer graphics. You watch a movie and half the time it looks like a video game cutscene. It just takes you right out of the story. I was watching this new sci-fi movie the other night, and the alien looked so fake I actually turned it off and just went to bed...

Hold on, what did you ask me? How long? Yeah, about a year. Ever since I got that safety award, that's when they all started acting weird and trying to mess with my reports.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that coworkers are acting weird and trying to sabotage their reports.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, wandering from a plaque to furniture assembly, DVDs, and movies before returning to the question.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from this specific situation at work, do you find that you have a hard time trusting people in general, or that you tend to suspect others of having hidden motives even when there isn't clear evidence?
turns.patient_response:
Trusting people in general? No, I've always been pretty trusting, honestly. I mean, I don't think everyone's out to get me or anything. Like I said, it's just the guys at the depot. But speaking of trust, I used to trust this one pizza place near my old apartment completely. Like, I would order from them every Friday night, same thing: large pepperoni, extra cheese, well-done. 

And for years, it was perfect. The crust had that perfect crunch, you know? But then they changed management or something, and suddenly the pizzas started arriving soggy. Like, the middle would just flop over when you picked up a slice, and all the toppings would slide right off onto the plate. It's the worst when that happens. You try to scoop it back up with a fork, but it's just not the same as biting into a solid slice. I tried calling them to complain once, and the kid on the phone sounded like he was about twelve years old. He didn't even know what I meant by "well-done." How do you work at a pizza place and not know that? 

I ended up having to buy one of those pizza stones for my oven so I could just reheat their sloppy pizzas and crisp up the bottom myself. Those stones are incredibly heavy, by the way. I dropped mine on my toe once while I was washing it in the sink. Bruised the nail right through, turned completely black. I had to wear open-toed sandals for a week, which is not a great look for me, especially in November. It was freezing...

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Hidden motives? No, no. Outside of work, I trust people fine. I'm not paranoid or anything. It's just the situation at the depot that's messed up.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient reiterates a fixed, persecutory belief specifically regarding 'the guys at the depot' being against him.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits marked tangentiality, going off on a long, unrelated story about pizza, a pizza stone, and a bruised toe before returning to the doctor's question.
